newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Kidnappers seize niece of top Colombian judge.
newsitem.headline: Kidnappers seize niece of top Colombian judge.

text.p: A massive police and army search was launched in northwest Colombia after unidentified kidnappers snatched the 13-year-old niece of a top judge early on Tuesday, the head of the anti-kidnap police said.

Col. Jesus Antonio Bohorquez, chief of the GAULA anti-kidnap squad, said Ana Maria Argueyes might have been abducted to prepare for the possible release of her father, held by kidnappers for more than two years.

"All police and army anti-kidnap groups are searching Antioquia (province) for this youngster. On many occasions -- for questions of health, for example -- kidnappers swap their prisoners," Bohorquez said.

The girl's father is Martin Alberto Argueyes, a businessman who was kidnapped by common criminals, police sources said. She was seized by three armed men as she waited for a school bus in the industrial city of Medellin.

She is the niece of Carlos Gaviria Diaz, chairman of Colombia's Constitutional Court, which is considering aspects of a controversial move to lift Colombia's ban on extradition. But Gaviria said he did not believe the kidnapping was linked to the review.
In the late 1980s and early 1990s, drug barons staged kidnappings and bombings in a successful bid to force a constituional ban on extradition, which took effect in 1991.

"The girl's mother is my half sister and I don't think the kidnappers would have been aware of the relationship. I don't think this has anything at all to do with the work of the court," Gaviria said.

News of the kidnapping came shortly after the GAULA force freed a 14-year-old girl on Tuesday and won the release over the weekend of a 13-year-old cycling champion who had been held for 36 hours, both in Antioquia.
Colombia has the highest kidnapping rate in the world, with one person kidnapped every 2-1/2 hours, security experts say.
